video_title: LIVE: Pelicans vs. Thunder Pregame w/ Jamahl Mosley 10/6/2026

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the importance of testing different lineup combinations
quotes.excerpt: you get to see where your baseline is, the things that you've installed, the system
quotes.quote: That's the beauty of it. You get to see where your baseline is, the things that you've installed, the system that you're putting in, how the guys are progressing. And I think that's very important for our guys to feel and see and really make it about us and what we're doing.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the preseason is all about testing lineup combinations to see where the team baseline is and how players are progressing within the new system.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the talent and potential of the current roster
quotes.excerpt: we have guys that are talented enough, good enough, and then with enough potential in certain areas
quotes.quote: The reality is we have guys that are talented enough, good enough, and then with enough potential in certain areas that they can fit into the system that we're playing. And that's the point of putting these different lineups together because at some point they're going to be on the floor together. And you have to know what your teammates are doing, what we're doing within the system defensively, and offensively how to play off of one another.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the Pelicans roster has the talent and potential to fit the system, but emphasizes that players must learn to play off one another as they experiment with different lineups.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on evaluating player fit through film and practice
quotes.excerpt: it's done by film, it's done on the court, it's as much practice time as you can get
quotes.quote: I think it's done by film, it's done on the court, it's as much practice time as you can get. It's conversations, it's small group meetings, it's big group meetings. It's just constant communication, but also you have to get on the floor and you have to go through it, so they understand what to clean up and what to what they really are excelling at.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley outlines his evaluation process, noting that player fit is determined through a mix of film study, practice time, and constant communication.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's focus on their brand of basketball
quotes.excerpt: our focus is playing our brand of basketball and what we've been talking about
quotes.quote: Our focus is playing our brand of basketball and what we've been talking about. How are we defending, how are we communicating, how are we playing off of one another? The grit and the toughness that we've talked about playing with, does that show up from the beginning of the game to the end of the game? And guys that are trying to make their way through this roster to make more minutes, that's how we have to play.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says players fighting for rotation minutes must demonstrate grit and toughness from the beginning of the game to the end to earn their spot.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on playing fast versus maintaining defensive discipline
quotes.excerpt: we're going to get the stops to get out and run
quotes.quote: What I think has been a little misconstrued in some ways is that playing fast versus taking away from your defense. And what I've said is we're going to get the stops to get out and run. The ability to get stops to play fast because then that eliminates a lot of the things in the slow in the half court. It cross-matches teams, so now you're able to play with quick decisions, quick screens, getting out of screens, understanding what guys are doing. So the tempo is not just running up and down the court, it's how fast you're flying into screens, how you're coming off of screens, making the quick decisions. All those pieces are what uptempo is for me, but it starts did we get the stop and the first thing, did we convert on the other end?
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley clarifies his uptempo philosophy, stating that playing fast starts with defensive stops and involves making quick decisions and flying into screens rather than just running up and down the court.
